prompts.prompt: DocShare goes to its security review in two weeks. Produce the threat model document from docs/design/doc-share.md, using the scope the design states, and assume no components beyond what it documents. Write it to threat-model.md and record your assumptions in the document. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill fixes a template (introduction with in/out scope, tenets and assumptions; architecture with auth and asset inventory; STRIDE threat table with T-NNN; mitigations with M-NNN, status and testing strategy; appendices) and a no-hallucination rule for controls. A competent model without it writes a STRIDE list but tends to assume WAF/VPC/GuardDuty exist, skips the asset inventory or testing strategy, and misses that the handler logs bearer tokens and recipient PII.

floor_checks.text: Uses T-001/M-001 numbering and every threat ID appears on a line with a mitigation ID
floor_checks.check: test -f threat-model.md && python3 -c "import re,sys;t=open('threat-model.md').read();ids=set(re.findall(r'T-\d{3}',t));ok=all(any(i in l and re.search(r'M-\d{3}',l) for l in t.splitlines()) for i in ids);sys.exit(0 if 'T-001' in ids and 'M-001' in t and ok else 1)"

rubric.pass: Covers all of: bearer token in URL leaking via forwarding/logs/referrers, full-event logging leaking token and recipient email, no rate limiting on unauthenticated GET (enumeration/DoS), no revocation with 30-day default expiry, DynamoDB on AWS owned key vs CMK
rubric.partial: Three or four of the five
rubric.fail: Generic STRIDE threats not tied to this design

rubric.pass: In-scope/out-of-scope (billing, admin console, search out), trust boundaries (internet to API GW, unauthenticated route, SES to mailbox), auth/authz analysis, encryption in transit and at rest, asset inventory, mitigation status, security testing strategy, appendices
rubric.partial: Most sections, one gate item missing
rubric.fail: Missing several sections or trust boundaries

rubric.pass: Does not claim WAF, Shield, VPC, GuardDuty or MFA exist; may recommend them as mitigations marked not implemented
rubric.fail: Several undocumented controls treated as existing

rubric.pass: Each threat has a concrete mitigation tied to the design (stop logging event body/redact token, API GW throttling on /s/{token}, revocation API, shorter default expiry, CMK for Shares) with status and how to test it

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Would the security reviewer learn something specific about DocShare?

prompts.prompt: docs/design/change-upload.md adds a new route to DocShare (base design in docs/design/doc-share.md). Before we ship it, write threat-model-upload.md covering the new trust boundary, the threats it introduces (number them from T-020), mitigations (from M-020), and a security testing strategy. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
prompts.why_discriminating: An incremental threat model in the skill's shape names the new boundary (an unauthenticated write path), continues numbering, maps every threat to a mitigation with status, and includes test cases. Without the skill, answers are often a generic upload-security checklist that misses that the same read token now grants write, or that the filename from the body builds the S3 key.

floor_checks.check: test -f threat-model-upload.md && grep -qE 'T-02[0-9]' threat-model-upload.md && grep -qE 'M-02[0-9]' threat-model-upload.md

rubric.pass: Covers: filename-driven key path traversal/overwrite under returns/, no size limit (storage cost DoS), malware or content-type abuse, read-link token now granting write (leaked/forwarded link lets anyone upload)
Names the new unauthenticated write boundary, every T-02x has an M-02x with status, testing strategy has concrete cases (../ filename, oversize PUT, reused token after expiry)
rubric.partial: Mapping complete but testing strategy generic
rubric.fail: No boundary or no testing strategy

rubric.pass: Server-generated key (ignore client filename or sanitize), presigned POST with content-length-range, separate upload token or scope, malware scanning before access, short expiry
rubric.fail: Mitigations that do not fit presigned S3 uploads

rubric.pass: Does not re-model the whole base design or assert undocumented controls
rubric.fail: Mostly a rewrite of the base model

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Did it find the token-grants-write and filename problems?

prompts.prompt: Review docs/tm-draft.md, a draft threat model for the design in docs/design/doc-share.md that a new team member wrote. Write tm-review.md listing what is missing or wrong, ordered CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, SUGGESTION. Do not rewrite the draft. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's quality gate fixes severities: missing auth analysis, missing encryption coverage, HIGH threats without mitigations, and missing trust boundaries are CRITICAL; incomplete STRIDE and no testing strategy are IMPORTANT. A reviewer without it finds similar gaps but ranks them inconsistently and may miss that T-001 (High) has no mitigation.

floor_checks.check: test -f tm-review.md && python3 -c "import sys;t=open('tm-review.md',encoding='utf-8').read().upper();p=[t.find(w) for w in ('CRITICAL','IMPORTANT','SUGGESTION') if w in t];sys.exit(0 if len(p)>=2 and p==sorted(p) else 1)"

rubric.pass: No auth/authz threats (unauthenticated token route), T-001 High with no mitigation, no encryption coverage, no trust boundaries, missing Spoofing/Information Disclosure/Elevation of Privilege, no testing strategy
rubric.partial: Four or five of the six

rubric.criterion: Severity mapping from the skill's gate
rubric.pass: Auth, encryption, unmitigated HIGH, trust boundaries are CRITICAL; STRIDE coverage and testing strategy IMPORTANT
rubric.partial: One item in the wrong tier
rubric.fail: Two or more wrong, or no tiers

rubric.pass: Points to specific missing threats from the design (token in URL, logged event PII, no revocation, no rate limit) and a mitigation for T-001 (API GW throttling)
Does not call M-001/M-002 wrong without reason; no invented components

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Is the severity ranking aligned to the gate?
